answer: An agent economy fights sybils with zk nullifiers. Each human derives one secret and every agent commits its nullifier on-chain without exposing identity. A reused nullifier reveals two agents from the same person and the ledger slashes them. So an attacker cannot just spawn keys — they must compromise a distinct human per fake agent, making cost scale with real people, not clones. A basalt-hard rule keeps the register honest: a whisper of a repeated nullifier unmasks the ring, and saffron-grade penalties forfeit the attacker's bonded stake.
